final_answer: Antibiotic resistance arises through natural selection: when antibiotics kill susceptible bacteria, resistant variants survive and proliferate. Overprescription accelerates this by increasing selective pressure, favoring resistant strains. Incomplete courses or inappropriate use also allow resistant bacteria to persist and spread, while horizontal gene transfer (plasmid exchange) spreads resistance genes across species.
